quote: Well, Hartenstraat is a side street of the Herengracht. That's not far from the palace on the Dam.

note: Jonas's school
quote: In Ludwigshafen, at the Rhein School.

quote: So my eldest brother, he married in Nuremberg, and my second brother, he married in Berlin.

quote: We were very orthodox at that time.

quote: My older brother was called Salomon and he helped in the business.

quote: They call them ear irons. Ear irons yes.

quote: And he describes that shul in the Nieuwe Kerkstraat. That was the so-called Russian Shul.

quote: On Gipsstrasse, also in the center of the city, near the Hackescher Markt.

quote: A small business, but my mother, even in Ludwigshafen, my mother went into the countryside, also in Ludwigshafen.

name: 30 January 1933
note: Hitler comes to power
quote: January 30th, 1933, Hitler came.

note: Marcus beaten by the SA in the Berlin courthouse
quote: In April, or was it March, maybe, 1933, he was beaten up beaten into a pulp in the courthouse in Berlin.

name: Courthouse, Berlin-Mitte
note: Where Marcus was beaten
quote: In April, or was it March, maybe, 1933, he was beaten up beaten into a pulp in the courthouse in Berlin.

quote: I have a photo. There's also a photo of my brother.

quote: In the meantime, my brother from Nuremberg had already left in 1932

quote: He said, I'm going, I'm going to Holland. The Hague. To live

quote: So we did the same thing. We also took the train to the Netherlands.

quote: The train ticket was for Berlin to Antwerp.

quote: At the border at Oldenzaal, our brother who already lived here came to meet us.

name: Warhaftig

quote: She also lived in Berlin. She was married with Warhaftig. And they came to the Netherlands a few months later as well.

quote: On Schelderstraat. Later we lived on Radiolaan. Then everything was gone.

name: Radiolaan, Den Haag
note: Later address
quote: On Schelderstraat. Later we lived on Radiolaan. Then everything was gone.

name: Palestine

quote: First I tried something else because I already wanted to go to Palestine then.

note: British-issued permit; hard to get
quote: That didn't work. It was very difficult because you couldn't get a certificate, and then you had to go to hachshara.

name: Hachshara
note: Agricultural training for emigrants to Palestine
quote: That didn't work. It was very difficult because you couldn't get a certificate, and then you had to go to hachshara.

name: Augusta Stemmer-Better

quote: In the meantime, my mother had died young, 54 years old.

name: end of 1937
note: Jonas gets engaged
quote: And at the end of '37 I got engaged, beginning of '38 maybe, end of '37.

name: Dora Stemmer
note: Met in Scheveningen (named on tape 2 at 0:51)
quote: Where did you meet your wife?

name: Gentsestraat, Scheveningen

name: IJmuiderstraat, Scheveningen
note: In-laws' bakery
quote: The bakery was on IJmuiderstraat.

note: November 1938 pogrom
quote: Kristalnacht

quote: On a Sunday, I went to get something. Suddenly I saw on the street SA men who wore those white armbands with 'Hilfspolizei' written on them.

quote: Well, then in '33. My brother, yes, in '35 my second brother Marcus Mordecai went. He went with his wife and child, with his son and they got a certificate.

name: Jewish Agency
note: Issued immigration certificates
quote: That's how he got a certificate, because from the Jewish Agency it was very difficult to get the certificate.

name: 1 September 1939
note: War breaks out
quote: And in 1939, the war broke out. September, September 1st, 1939, right.

name: Chile

quote: That brother-in-law of my brother who lived here, my oldest brother's brother-in-law, he already went - he was a Dutchman - he already went with his whole family to Chile.

note: Salomon leaves for Chile by boat via Trieste
quote: And he left December 4th, '39. December 4th, '39 to Chile by boat via Trieste, Italy.

name: Trieste
note: Port of departure to Chile
quote: And he left December 4th, '39. December 4th, '39 to Chile by boat via Trieste, Italy.

name: Rotterdam

quote: Then it was, so they had a business and that was taken over by a firm in Rotterdam, Mr. Hartog, he took over that business and appointed me as manager in The Hague.

name: Chuppah
note: Jewish wedding canopy
quote: The chuppah, do you know what that is? I had the chuppah, December 31st, '39, the last day of the year.

name: 31 December 1939
note: Jonas's wedding
quote: The chuppah, do you know what that is? I had the chuppah, December 31st, '39, the last day of the year.

quote: Early March '40.

quote: I got an order from Haas Fashion.

name: April 1940
note: Jonas takes over the business
quote: Yes, you can find it in the Chamber of Commerce. It's all written precisely that I took over a business from Mr. Hartog, and that was in April.

note: German invasion of the Netherlands, Friday morning
quote: May 10th was a Friday morning.

name: Dora Stemmer
note: Jonas's wife, called "Do"
quote: I told my wife 'Do (Dora), it's war'.

note: Planes with the German cross over The Hague
quote: Well, a few minutes later more came and I suddenly saw that cross - you know, the German one - on the airplane. Well, it's over. This is it. It's war.

name: Distribution radio (radiodistributie)
note: Wired radio service
quote: And we had a distribution radio then. Do you know what that is?

name: Den Haag
note: Paratroopers land around The Hague
quote: In the area of The Hague, parachutists have come down.

name: 10 May 1939
note: Civil marriage, to qualify for the US quota

quote: The reason was, I wanted to go to America.

name: Sudetenland
note: Dora's birthplace, later Czechoslovakia
quote: And my wife was born in the Sudetenland which belonged then... when she was born, I don't know if that belonged to Germany.

name: Scheveningen
note: They stay with the in-laws until 14 May
quote: Well, '40. We went to my parents to my parents-in-law we went, to Scheveningen.

name: Scheveningen Pier
note: Where they watched the smoke over Rotterdam
quote: We saw the pier we were standing there. Then you suddenly saw after 2 hours, between 2 and 3 o'clock, you already saw the smoke clouds from Rotterdam

name: Rotterdam
note: Bombed on 14 May 1940
quote: We saw the pier we were standing there. Then you suddenly saw after 2 hours, between 2 and 3 o'clock, you already saw the smoke clouds from Rotterdam

quote: We saw the pier we were standing there. Then you suddenly saw after 2 hours, between 2 and 3 o'clock, you already saw the smoke clouds from Rotterdam

quote: We saw the pier we were standing there. Then you suddenly saw after 2 hours, between 2 and 3 o'clock, you already saw the smoke clouds from Rotterdam

note: Born 15 July 1941; name not given

quote: It was an agency, a German agency, that was on the Korte Vijverberg here in The Hague.

quote: And they sent a form every month during the course of '41, '42 to fill in whether we could do any work for the Wehrmacht.

name: Verwalter (administrator)

quote: And they sent a form every month during the course of '41, '42 to fill in whether we could do any work for the Wehrmacht.

note: With 3 daughters and twin grandchildren aged 3
quote: But yes, I had family here. My in-laws with 3 daughters, 2 grandchildren, twins of 3 years old.

name: Rosa Stemmer
note: His sister, with 4 children, stays behind

note: Stays behind with Jonas's stepmother
quote: I have my sister with 4 children, my father with my stepmother.

name: Stepmother of Jonas
note: Name not given
quote: I have my sister with 4 children, my father with my stepmother.

quote: I made contact with a woman in the city, on Rembrandtstraat, who would bring us to Belgium.

quote: And we left Wednesday morning, June 24th, 1942. It was a very warm day. A coat with some clothes and a bag.

note: Compulsory for Jews from May 1942

name: Nieuwe Schoolstraat, Den Haag
note: Their home, near Hollands Spoor
quote: We didn't live far from the station, the Holland Spoor station on the Nieuwe Schoolstraat.

quote: And then we arrived in Bergen op Zoom.

name: Tallit and tefillin

note: Smuggled across on foot

quote: And we arrived at a small station, and there was a small train to Antwerp.

name: Antwerpen-Centraal station
note: He lost the tickets and slipped past control
quote: Then it goes down like this, the stairs going down.

name: Jewish quarter, Antwerp
note: Dora's relatives; they stay about a week
quote: My wife had distant family or something she knew in Antwerp in the Jewish neighborhood.

name: Belgian star ("J")
note: Different from the Dutch "Jood" star
quote: Stars in Belgium are different from in the Netherlands.

name: Brussels
note: Dora's cousin
quote: Then we went to my wife's cousin, in Brussels.

name: Vichy France (unoccupied zone)
note: Their goal
quote: Our goal was to get to so-called 'unoccupied France.'

name: Smugglers (passeurs)
note: 2 smugglers, 12 refugees
quote: We found smugglers if you know what that is.

name: Charleville-Mézières
note: Border town; they walk there overnight
quote: There's a border town, Mézières Charleville.

name: Dora Stemmer
note: Goes by train with the baby and a local woman
quote: And my wife with the child went by train that bit with a woman, Belgian or French, I don't know exactly.

note: Train change
quote: We had to transfer. We stopped in Reims and arrived in Paris on Friday afternoon.

name: Paris
note: Arrive Friday afternoon; a forbidden zone
quote: We had to transfer. We stopped in Reims and arrived in Paris on Friday afternoon.

name: German soldiers in the hotel
note: Paris hotel
quote: By the way, there were German soldiers in that hotel too.

name: Gare d'Austerlitz, Paris
note: Train south on Sunday morning
quote: Not far, I don't remember how far it was, maybe 100 100 or 200 meters or so to the metro. We went to Gare d'Austerlitz.

name: Tours
note: Middle of France
quote: We went to Tours, middle of France.

name: Vel' d'Hiv roundup

quote: On that Sunday was the biggest roundup in Paris, July 1942.

name: July 1942
note: Biggest roundup in Paris
quote: On that Sunday was the biggest roundup in Paris, July 1942.

note: Border between occupied and unoccupied France
quote: That was about, I think, 50 or 60 kilometers from the line of demarcation, the border between occupied and unoccupied France.

quote: Then we ended up in a small village, or hamlet, where you'd only see German soldiers.

quote: Then a couple comes towards us with a baby carriage. And one of the people who were with us, there were two brothers, twins. What were their names again, I've forgotten? They spoke good French. They came from Brussels, most were from Belgium anyway.

name: Belgian farmer
note: Shelters the group on his farm
quote: He was a Belgian farmer.

name: Belgian farmer's farm near the demarcation line
note: They sleep in a haystack
quote: He was a Belgian farmer.

name: Crossing the demarcation line
note: Night walk from 10:30 pm to 6 am through the forest
quote: We started walking, until 4 o'clock in the morning. From 10:30.

name: Large farm in the unoccupied zone
note: Food and milk after the crossing

quote: And that smuggler, the agreement was that he would bring us from Brussels to Lyon.

name: Small station in the unoccupied zone
note: Horse cart to the train
quote: Not a car. A horse cart.

name: Gendarmes

quote: We got on the train and suddenly we saw, the train made a stop. We saw those 7 who got into the second car being pulled out by the gendarmes.

name: Limoges
note: Big station; "porcelain city"
quote: The train went on. We arrived in Limoges.

name: Lyon
note: Destination; night train from Limoges
quote: And we wanted to go to Lyon.

name: July 1942
note: Arrival in Lyon after 12 hours on the train
quote: We arrived in Lyon at 1 o'clock in the afternoon.

name: Sister of Salomon's wife
note: Lyon contact; left Antwerp in 1940
quote: We had an address. It was a sister of my sister-in-law, my brother's wife who went to Chile.

name: Restaurant "Am Brun", Lyon
note: Meeting place for Dutch refugees. Name as heard; to verify

name: Berent Bekker
note: Friend from The Hague, met in Lyon
quote: So I go to restaurant Am Brun. You could find more people from Holland there. I left my wife there for a moment. I went there and I met a friend of mine, Berent Bekker, from The Hague.

name: Hôtel Saint-Pothin, rue Saint-Pothin, Lyon
note: First lodging; shared a room for a week
quote: Go to hotel St. Pothin, the street is also called St. Pothin. Maybe he has a place for you.

name: Niece of Jonas (Kern family)
note: From Brussels; arrives in Lyon with husband and son
quote: That was the beginning when we arrived. Then the niece I told you about from Brussels also unfortunately came with her husband and son to Lyon.

name: Raids in Lyon
note: Roundups of foreign Jews, summer 1942
quote: And then the raids began.

name: Office Néerlandais
note: Dutch office aiding refugees in unoccupied France
quote: Meanwhile I already had, yes, I already had the so-called passport, a pass, it was a document from the Office Néerlandais and Sally Noach

name: Sally Noach
note: Helped Dutch refugees in Lyon; got Jonas his pass
quote: Meanwhile I already had, yes, I already had the so-called passport, a pass, it was a document from the Office Néerlandais and Sally Noach

name: Office Néerlandais pass
note: Document confirming Jonas was Dutch
quote: Meanwhile I already had, yes, I already had the so-called passport, a pass, it was a document from the Office Néerlandais and Sally Noach

note: Second lodging, full of refugees
quote: We lived in a hotel, from there we had to leave St. Potin and we came to a hotel called Quai Jair. On the water.

quote: At 1, 1:30. The National Police came. 'Open the door'.

quote: And we were brought to the Sûreté. I don't know what it is. The main police headquarters.

quote: And there in front of me was [Klaus] Barbie, sitting there.

quote: And then people were then divided. 'Camp' in French, also 'camp de travail.'

name: Auschwitz
note: Destination of the first group
quote: Later we heard that camp went directly to Drancy, went to Auschwitz.

quote: I still have the answer with me.

note: Needed to leave France via Spain
quote: Because even if you had that, you had to have a visa de sortie and a transit visa.

quote: And then I went to the consulate of Spain and to the French.

quote: On Saturday there was a camp outside Lyon. It was a barracks of Indo-Chinese.

name: Niece of Jonas (Kern family)
note: She perished
quote: So the next day, that was on Sunday, that roundup... the price of it all... she perished in the struggle, and the other one, my nephew with that boy, they survived until the end. They met someone.

name: Buchenwald
note: Husband and son worked there
quote: They worked in Buchenwald, and in Buchenwald they had to march, had to go back. And that father and that son were on that road.

name: Death march
note: Husband shot; son survived
quote: They worked in Buchenwald, and in Buchenwald they had to march, had to go back. And that father and that son were on that road.

name: Vienna
note: Where the surviving son lives
quote: That father was shot dead, and that son who lives, he still lives in Vienna.

name: Switzerland
note: New escape goal
quote: Switzerland too, but well, you had to have a travel permit to be able to ride the train. That was from Lyon to Annemasse.

name: Annemasse
note: French border town opposite Geneva
quote: Switzerland too, but well, you had to have a travel permit to be able to ride the train. That was from Lyon to Annemasse.

name: Geneva
note: Across the border
quote: Switzerland too, but well, you had to have a travel permit to be able to ride the train. That was from Lyon to Annemasse.

name: Travel permit (sauf-conduit)
note: Lyon–Annemasse, stating "Protestant"
quote: I went to the police with a form, with a pack of cigarettes, and the next... well, in the afternoon I believe, I was allowed to pick it up.

name: Passeur (border smuggler)
note: About 200 francs to cross
quote: It cost something like 200 francs, I believe.

name: Route Nationale, French–Swiss border near Annemasse
note: Road with France on one side, Switzerland on the other
quote: And that man, the smuggler... the place was called Route Nationale. This side was Switzerland and this side was France.

name: Gendarmerie post near Annemasse
note: Night of interrogations
quote: Then we came to the gendarmerie post.

name: Tallit and tefillin
note: Still with him at the interrogation
quote: I had my Talit and Tfilin with me.

name: Rivesaltes
note: Internment and transit camp in southern France
quote: So they'd tell... the woman, those 2 daughters, the next day they came to Rivesaltes.

name: Alsace
note: A Swiss/French guard who spoke German
quote: I heard one of them. there was no road. I could speak German. He was from Alsace.

name: Swiss Red Cross
note: Jonas pleads for his wife and sick child
quote: 'Maybe it's possible that the Swiss Red Cross can take the womean and child.'

name: Receipt for confiscated money
note: Jonas says he still has it
quote: They then took everything we had and all our money from us, I still have the receipt of that.

name: Lyon
note: Ordered back to report to the police
quote: That same gendarme who stopped us the very first time came to pick us up at 3:30. We had to go back to Lyon.

name: Barbed-wire gap, French–Swiss border
note: Jonas spots a gap behind the stairs
quote: We walked a bit. I saw a house standing on the right side, and then stairs going up. Those stairs were still on the French side, and after the stairs was barbed wire.

name: Swiss customs officer
note: Leads them over the border
quote: By a Swiss customs officer.

name: Swiss gendarmerie post near Geneva
note: They wait for permission to stay
quote: to a Swiss gendarmerie post, or something like that.

name: Swiss border rejections
note: Families with children were admitted; thousands of others sent back
quote: we were lucky that we had the child with us.

name: early September 1942
note: Arrival in Switzerland, about 3 days before Rosh Hashanah
quote: This was September, the beginning of September.

name: Rosh Hashanah
note: Jewish New Year
quote: three days before Rosh Hashanah, if I am not mistaken.

name: Varembé reception camp, Geneva
note: Slept on straw. Transcribed as "Warembé"
quote: We were taken by car to a reception camp, Warembé, near Geneva.

name: Geneva
note: Small hotel near the station
quote: We were taken by car to Geneva, to a small hotel near the station.

name: Children's home and hospital, Geneva
note: Son in hospital for two months
quote: We went straight to a children's home to ask if they would take our child in for a while.

name: Yom Kippur
note: Spent in Geneva
quote: During Yom Kippur we were still there.

name: Sukkot
note: Invited by a Swiss Jewish family
quote: A Family had already told us since you are here, you will be with us for Sukkoth. They were Swiss Jews.

name: Genève-Cornavin station
note: Ordered to report with 120 others
quote: Cornavin station.

name: Threat of expulsion
note: Geneva police: "You are not a Dutchman"; ends well
quote: Suddenly, while we were at the hotel, we received a summons to appear before the police.

name: Eriswil
note: End of the line; camp in an old school
quote: We arrived in a small place called Eriswil.

name: Letters from the Geneva hospital
note: Jonas says he still has them
quote: I still have all the letters from that hospital in Geneva.

name: Bienenberg internment home, near Liestal
note: Dora and the child; an old hotel
quote: They went to an internment home called Bienenberg, near Liestal, not far from Basel.

name: Basel
note: Near Liestal
quote: They went to an internment home called Bienenberg, near Liestal, not far from Basel.

name: Son of Jonas
note: In five or six hospitals until November 1945
quote: In those four years, until November 1945, he was in five or six hospitals.

name: March/April 1943
note: Jonas transferred
quote: In any case, in '43, March or April, I don't know exactly.

name: Adliswil
note: Camp near Zurich
quote: I was transferred to Adliswil. 1943

name: Identity card from the Dutch consulate in Bern
note: Jonas still has it
quote: I have my identity card from the Dutch consulate in Bern, and it is also recorded in my Swiss pass.

name: Swiss refugee pass
note: Records his camps
quote: And I also have my Swiss pass it's all recorded there.

name: Le Chaluet labour camp, near Moutier
note: Bernese Jura. Jonas got muscle rheumatism
quote: From Adliswil I went to the work camp Le Chaluet.

name: Photo of Le Chaluet
note: "You have seen the photo"
quote: You have seen the photo. That is Le Chaluet.

name: Raron labour camp
note: Near Brig, close to the Italian border
quote: After that I was moved to another work camp called Raron.

name: Baden
note: Spa near Zurich; sent for treatment
quote: Because I was ill, I got leave twice to go to Baden near Zurich, to take the baths.

name: Morgins internment camp
note: Valais, on the French border; Grand Hotel, Victoria, La Forêt
quote: Then I came to the internment camp Morgins. Morgin that is in.

note: Dora and the child join him at Morgins
quote: Only in 1944 did I manage to bring my wife and child there too.

name: Lausanne
note: One of the son's hospitals
quote: He was in hospital again. Lausanne, Zurich, Baden, Geneva.

name: May 1945
note: Liberation
quote: We still could not go home. The liberation was May 1945.

name: Statelessness
note: Not allowed back to the Netherlands as a non-Dutch citizen
quote: I was not allowed to return to the Netherlands, because I was not a Dutch citizen.

name: 7 November 1945
note: Return to the Netherlands, on Jonas's birthday
quote: To tell it briefly, we arrived on my birthday, November 7th, 1945.

name: Eindhoven
note: Arrival by train from Basel through France
quote: By train from Basel, through France, back to Holland, to Eindhoven.

name: Philips factory hall, Eindhoven
note: Reception and registration
quote: In the factory hall of Philips we slept there for a night. We registered.

name: Displaced person registration papers
note: Jonas still has them
quote: I still have those papers. Displaced person, I don't know what.

name: Jewish Brigade
note: Present in Eindhoven
quote: We had no house. In Eindhoven at that time was the Jewish Brigade.

name: Westerbork
note: A friend released because of his mixed marriage
quote: We had a good acquaintance who had a non-Jewish wife. He was in Westerbork but got out because of the mixed marriage.

name: Rijnstraat, Amsterdam
note: The friend's home; Dora and the children stay there
quote: He lived in Amsterdam on the Rijnstraat and wrote to us right after the war, when you arrive, come to us.

name: 29 May 1945
note: Second son born
quote: Meanwhile we also had a second child. He was born May 29th, 1945.

name: Second son of Jonas
note: Born 29 May 1945 in Montreux; name not given
quote: Meanwhile we also had a second child. He was born May 29th, 1945.

name: Montreux
note: Birthplace of the second son
quote: In Switzerland, in Montreux. We were up in the hills above Montreux.

name: Goudenregenstraat, Den Haag
note: Temporary city hall after the war
quote: The city hall was gone. It was now in the Goudenregenstraat.

name: Prins Mauritslaan, Den Haag
note: House run by the Jewish community; slept there
quote: On Prinsmauritslaan there was a house that had been managed by the Jewish community.

name: Hoefkade, Den Haag
note: Rented room
quote: I slept there. Then I got a room in the city, on the Hoefkade.

name: September 1942
note: Dora's parents and family are arrested
quote: And then there was the house of my parents-in-law, who had been taken away in September 1942.

name: Franz Fischer
note: "Judenfischer", SD officer in The Hague
quote: They were taken by that Judenfischer, Franz Fischer, that murderer.

name: Parents-in-law of Jonas
note: Arrested September 1942; murdered in Auschwitz
quote: They were taken by that Judenfischer, Franz Fischer, that murderer.

name: Belgisch Park, Scheveningen
note: Dora's sister and the twins arrested there
quote: In the Belgisch Park, you know it. Fischer walked past and arrested them.

name: Windekind, Scheveningen
note: Detention site; one night
quote: were brought to the Windekind. You know it too. They stayed there one night.

name: Auschwitz
note: Dora's family murdered within ten days
quote: They were classified as a punishment case. Within ten days they were dead in Auschwitz.

name: Repatriation debt
note: Billed for the return journey; 500 Swiss francs, paid off
quote: I came back. Not long after I received a notice from the Ministry,

name: Rosa Stemmer
note: Jonas's sister; deported to Sobibor with her four children in April (1943)
quote: My sister, in April, in April, with four children, was taken to Sobibor.

name: Sobibor
note: Rosa and her children; The Hague rabbis
quote: My sister, in April, in April, with four children, was taken to Sobibor.

name: David Loeb Stemmer
note: "The last transport", August 1943; to verify
quote: My father was on the last transport. That was August, August 1943.

name: 17th of Tammuz
note: Fast day; rabbis of The Hague deported
quote: I don't know if you know it, the 17th of Tammuz, a Jewish fast day.

name: Property management institute (Nederlands Beheersinstituut)
note: Post-war body managing Jewish property
quote: After the war a property management institute had been set up.

name: Rijswijk
note: The administrator was a teacher there
quote: He gave me the name. The administrator was a teacher in Rijswijk.

name: Photo of David Loeb and Augusta Stemmer
note: Shown on camera
quote: On the right is my father David Loeb Stemmer

name: David Loeb Stemmer
note: Jonas's father. Likely the "david stemmer" scans
quote: On the right is my father David Loeb Stemmer

name: Augusta Stemmer-Better
note: Jonas's mother
quote: On the left side, you can see my mother, Augusta Stemmer-Better.

name: Photo of David Loeb Stemmer, c. 1935–36
note: Taken in the Netherlands
quote: Look. The photo of my father was taken here in Holland, around 1935, 1936.

name: Family photo with Marcus's family
note: Taken before they left for Palestine, 1935
quote: Here you can see my brother, second from the left.

name: Mordechai (Marcus) Stemmer
note: Second from left in the photo
quote: Here you can see my brother, second from the left.

name: Professor Shamir
note: Marcus's son, professor in Jerusalem
quote: He is Professor Shamir from Jerusalem. And behind him stands my father.

name: Jerusalem
note: Where Marcus's family lives
quote: He is Professor Shamir from Jerusalem. And behind him stands my father.

name: Rosa Stemmer
note: His sister, with her husband, in the photo
quote: And my sister and my brother-in-law.

name: Sobibor
note: Some of those pictured perished there
quote: No, not all of them, some perished in Sobibor. The youngest one is my sister’s.
